transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

I guess… work has been getting harder. I keep having to go back over things I’ve already done—breakers, labels, torque marks, pictures, that kind of stuff. Sometimes I’ll even drive back to a site to check.

It’s making simple jobs take a lot longer than they should, and people are starting to notice.
Do you ever have thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that you find disturbing or unwanted, and that make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Yeah… I mean, I guess so.

Even when I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, I’ll get this thought that maybe I missed something—like one loose neutral, or something that could start a fire. I try to push it away, but it kind of sticks with me… sometimes all the way home.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, counting, or going back to make sure something’s done—to try to reduce the anxiety those thoughts cause?

Yeah. Mostly checking.

I’ll go back over breakers, labels, torque marks… photos too. Sometimes I’ll tell myself it’s fine, but then I end up checking again anyway. There’ve been times I’ve driven back to a site just to make sure.

It turns a simple install into something that takes way longer than it should. People are starting to notice.
When you go back to check things like breakers or labels, is it because you feel anxious that something bad might happen if you don’t, like a fire or an electrical problem?

Yeah… mostly. It’s that feeling that if I don’t look again, I might’ve missed something.

So I end up going back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, photos… sometimes even driving back. I know it sounds like a lot, but I can’t really settle until I’ve checked. Then the job takes way longer than it should.
Do these checking behaviors take up a lot of your time—like more than an hour a day—or cause you a lot of stress?

Yeah… it does. More than I’d like to admit.

It’s the checking that brings me in, really. I keep going back over jobs—breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—and sometimes I’ve even driven back to a site. A simple install ends up taking way longer than it should, and… people are starting to notice.

When you go back to check things like breakers or labels, does it have to be done a certain way or a certain number of times for you to feel okay, or is it more about making sure nothing bad happens like a fire?

It’s not really a certain number or ritual, no.

It’s more… I don’t trust that I caught everything. So I go back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos—sometimes I’ll even drive back to the site—just to make sure nothing’s wrong. It ends up dragging the job out, and people have noticed.

When you go back to check things, do you feel that something bad like a fire or electrical failure will definitely happen if you don't check, or is it more that you just can't shake the feeling that something might be wrong?

It’s not like I think it’ll definitely happen.

It’s more that I can’t get rid of the thought… like, even if I know I checked the panel or the disconnect, I keep thinking maybe I missed one loose neutral, or left something that could start a fire. I try to push it away, but sometimes it follows me all the way home.
Have you ever experienced other thoughts or behaviors that feel intrusive or repetitive, like counting, repeating words silently, or needing things to be in a specific order?

Not really counting or repeating words, no.

For me it’s mostly the work stuff… going back over the same job, checking breakers, labels, torque marks, photos. Sometimes even going back to the site. I know I’ve said that already, but that’s the thing that keeps looping.
When you go back to check breakers or labels, does it feel like you have to do it to prevent something really bad from happening, even if you know the chances are low?

Yeah… I guess that’s the part of it.

I know it’s probably not likely, but I keep thinking if I don’t go back over the breakers or the labels or the torque marks, I might miss something important. So I check the photos, sometimes go back to the site. It makes jobs take a lot longer than they should. People are starting to notice.
